name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,396

clue.text: Frenchwoman taking credit for daughter's handiwork

indicators.note: taking one thing for another means one letter is swapped out and another put in its place

blocks.note: the French title for a married woman
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman claims the credit for a piece of craftwork her daughter actually made.
explanation.walkthrough: In MADAME the D is replaced by CR, giving MACRAME.
explanation.definitionFit: Macramé is decorative knotted string or cord work, a traditional craft made by hand.

clue.text: Exploit of Mark touring Israel

indicators.note: a tourer travels around a place, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: Mk is the abbreviation for the old German mark
IL is the international country code for Israel

explanation.surface: Someone takes advantage of a man called Mark while he travels around Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: To milk someone or something is to exploit it, draining every possible advantage from it.

clue.text: Map out church mural?

blocks.note: CH is the standard abbreviation for church
a mural is an example of art, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: A question about planning a painting on a church wall.
explanation.definitionFit: To chart a course or territory is to plot it, setting it down on a map or plan.

clue.text: Worried about party supporting Birmingham Centre's story

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits underneath, so it follows the other
about means surrounding, so one word wraps round the joined pair

blocks.note: worried as in gnawed at; something that ate at you troubled you
the National Exhibition Centre near Birmingham
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Someone frets over a party held at a Birmingham venue, as an anecdote.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Exhibition Centre is a big conference venue outside Birmingham, known by its initials; in a down clue the supporting word sits below.
explanation.definitionFit: An anecdote is a short amusing tale about a real incident, so it is a kind of story.

clue.text: Scientific study of European settlement's good for Norway

indicators.note: one thing put in place of another, so a letter is swapped for a different one

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for European
a colony is a settlement abroad
G is the abbreviation for good
N is the international vehicle code for Norway

explanation.surface: A scientific report on a European colony and how it compares with Norway.
explanation.walkthrough: In COLONY the N is swapped for G, then E goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecology is the branch of biology studying how organisms relate to their environment.

clue.text: Clerics' disciples hit back first

indicators.note: going back means the word is read from its end to its start
first places this piece at the front of the answer

blocks.note: to rap is to strike sharply
followers can be called sons, spiritual heirs of a master

explanation.surface: The followers of some clergymen strike back first.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe on Clerics is surface dressing; the definition is the plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsons are parish priests in the Church of England, so they are clergymen.

clue.text: Something to secure flat piece of hair

blocks.note: a pad is slang for a flat or home
a lock is a curl or tress of hair

explanation.surface: Something to fix a flat strand of hair in place.
explanation.definitionFit: A padlock is a detachable lock used for fastening gates, bikes and lockers shut.

clue.text: Tool to copy digital data was returned

indicators.note: something returned comes back the way it went, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: to rip a CD or DVD is to copy its contents to a computer
taken as written

explanation.surface: A computer tool for copying files was sent back.
explanation.definitionFit: A ripsaw is a coarse-toothed saw used for cutting timber along the grain.

clue.text: Nation defending imperial measure after old boy becomes stubborn

indicators.note: after places the second part behind the first in the answer
a defender stands round what it protects, so one word surrounds the other

blocks.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
a state is a nation
IN is the abbreviation for inch, an imperial unit

explanation.surface: A country clings to imperial units after a former pupil turns obstinate.
explanation.definitionFit: Being obstinate means refusing to change one's mind, the same as being stubborn or mulish.

clue.text: Cold nurses agitated disreputable men

indicators.note: agitated means stirred up and shaken, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Unfriendly nurses become upset by some shady men.
explanation.definitionFit: Scoundrels are dishonest rogues, men of bad character or reputation.

clue.text: Old ale she brewed is something a landlord sells?

indicators.note: brewing mixes and transforms ingredients, so these letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A pub landlord flogs old ale that a woman brewed.
explanation.walkthrough: The landlord looks like a publican selling beer, but it is a property owner granting a lease.
explanation.definitionFit: A leasehold is tenure of property for a fixed term, which a property owner can sell to a tenant.

clue.text: Quickly take out sauce

indicators.note: out means removed, so this letter is dropped from the word

blocks.note: presto is the musical direction for a fast pace
R stands for recipe, Latin for take, on prescriptions

explanation.surface: An instruction to remove a sauce fast.
explanation.walkthrough: R on a prescription is short for Latin recipe, meaning take; dropping it from PRESTO leaves PESTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Pesto is an Italian pasta sauce made from basil, pine nuts, garlic, cheese and oil.

clue.text: Policeman captured by revolutionary reveals location of workers?

indicators.note: a revolution turns things round, so the word is read backwards
something captured is held inside, so one word goes within the other

blocks.note: to out someone is to reveal a secret about them
DI is a Detective Inspector

explanation.surface: A police officer seized by a rebel discloses where workers are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reveals' looks like a link word but supplies the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A studio is a room where an artist or photographer works, so it is a workplace.

clue.text: Cheering new development getting rid of pub

indicators.note: getting rid of means removing, so these letters are dropped

blocks.note: an innovation is something newly introduced
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: People cheer a new scheme that does away with the local pub.
explanation.definitionFit: An ovation is sustained applause and acclaim from an audience, the noun for collective cheering.

clue.text: It may have been used by Mark Twain?

definitions.text: It may have been used by Mark Twain?

blocks.clueFragment: It may have been used by Mark Twain?
blocks.note: surface reading: some object the American author owned
setter's reading: Twain was a writer and an early adopter of the machine writers used to produce typed manuscripts

explanation.walkthrough: Mark Twain was one of the first authors to submit a typed manuscript; the answer also splits as a writer of a certain type.
explanation.definitionFit: The machine for printing letters onto paper by keys was used by authors such as Twain to produce manuscripts.

clue.text: Idle talk of sentry regularly carried by oxen

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken
something carried is held within, so it sits inside the other pieces

blocks.note: a yak is a long-haired ox; two of them make the plural
the even letters of the word
the second ox

explanation.surface: Idle chatter from a guard, carried along by oxen.
explanation.walkthrough: The oxen are a pair of yaks, one on each side of the selected letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Yakety-yak is informal for trivial, incessant chatter, an idiom for idle talk.

clue.text: Reportedly stops quality roadside fixture

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the word is judged by sound

blocks.note: curbs means stops or restrains
tone is a quality, as of sound or colour

explanation.surface: A report on how a quality kerb blocks the road.
explanation.walkthrough: Kerb is the British spelling of the pavement edge (US curb).
explanation.definitionFit: A kerbstone is one of the stone blocks forming the raised edge of a pavement beside a road.

clue.text: Look - sloth runs

blocks.note: the ai is the three-toed sloth, a crossword regular
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Look out: a sloth is running.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is a sloth that runs; the dash just separates definition from wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a manner or appearance, as in having an air of confidence, so it is a look.

clue.text: Standard piece of rock salmon

indicators.note: a piece is only a small part, so just one letter is taken

blocks.note: par is the standard or normal level
the opening letter

explanation.surface: An ordinary bit of rock salmon, which is a fish-shop name for dogfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock salmon' reads as one fish, but rock gives a letter and salmon is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A parr is a young salmon in its first freshwater stage, before it becomes a smolt.

clue.text: Lusted fancifully when embracing Doctor Fell

indicators.note: fanciful means imaginative and unrealistic, so the letters are freely rearranged
to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so one piece wraps round the other

blocks.note: taken as written
MB is a Bachelor of Medicine degree

explanation.surface: Someone lusted wildly after embracing Doctor Fell, the man in the nursery rhyme 'I do not like thee, Doctor Fell'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor Fell' reads as a name; Doctor gives letters and Fell, a verb, is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To stumble is to trip and nearly or actually fall, so stumbled can mean fell.

clue.text: Time to include final character in book

indicators.note: including something means holding it within, so one goes inside the other

blocks.note: an era is a period of time
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Time to put the last character into a novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Ezra is a book of the Old Testament, named after the Jewish priest and scribe.

clue.text: Means of state execution

blocks.note: surface reading: a method by which the state puts prisoners to death
setter's reading: execution as in formally executing a document, which this item authenticates on behalf of the sovereign

explanation.walkthrough: Execution here is the signing and sealing of official documents, not capital punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: The monarch's official seal is fixed to important state papers to make them legally valid.

clue.text: Legal documents in which old king replaces sovereign's bribes

indicators.note: one thing replacing another means it is swapped into the other's spot

blocks.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George
leases are rental contracts
L is the pound sign, and a sovereign is a gold pound coin

explanation.surface: Contracts in which a former monarch takes the place of the reigning one involve backhanders.
explanation.walkthrough: A sovereign is an old gold coin worth one pound, abbreviated L; in LEASES it is replaced by GR.
explanation.definitionFit: Greasing someone's palm means bribing them, so greases are bribes.

clue.text: Call without entitlement

blocks.note: ex is Latin for out of or without, as in ex dividend
a claim is a right or entitlement

explanation.surface: Calling out for something one has no right to.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclaim is to cry out suddenly, so it is to call out loudly.

clue.text: Body of rector found in wood

indicators.note: something found in a place lies inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for rector
a copse is a small wood

explanation.surface: A murder mystery: the vicar's body discovered among the trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Body of rector' reads as a single phrase, but Body alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A corpse is a dead body, especially a human one.

clue.text: Give back foreign currency after holiday

indicators.note: after puts this piece behind the other one in the answer

blocks.note: a rest is a break or holiday
the öre is a coin of Sweden, the øre of Denmark and Norway

explanation.surface: Handing back unused foreign money after a trip abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore something is to return it to its owner or former state.

clue.text: Commander's working routine

blocks.note: Comm. is an abbreviation for commander
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A commander goes about his everyday duties.
explanation.definitionFit: Common means ordinary or everyday, so a common occurrence is a routine one.

clue.text: Joke about hybrid is a gas

indicators.note: about means around, so one word surrounds the other

blocks.note: as in 'have you heard the one about...', a one is a joke
a zo or dzo is a cross between a yak and a cow

explanation.surface: A joke about a hybrid car is a laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is a gas' looks like slang for being great fun, but a gas is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozone is a form of oxygen with three atoms per molecule, a pungent gas found in the upper atmosphere.

clue.text: Requests to sunbathe topless on square

indicators.note: without its top, so the first letter is lost
in a down clue one piece placed on another sits above it

blocks.note: to bask is to lie in the sun
S is the abbreviation for square

explanation.surface: Requests to sunbathe without a top on in the town square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' suggests a sunbather, but it removes the first letter of BASK.
explanation.definitionFit: To ask is to make a request, so the verb form asks matches requests.

clue.text: Group of people, left eating nothing, retired

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so one piece goes within the other
retired means drawn back, so the whole is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: port is the left-hand side of a ship
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A group of people who left without eating anything and went to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A troop is a band or company of people, such as soldiers or scouts.

clue.text: Horses' loins rubbed with salt

indicators.note: rubbing works things together and scrambles them, so the letters get rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Horses having their flanks rubbed down with salt.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe on Horses is surface dressing; the definition is plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Stallions are uncastrated adult male horses kept for breeding.

clue.text: Jackets for midshipmen

blocks.note: first meaning: thick double-breasted jackets of the kind worn by sailors
second meaning: old naval slang for junior officers, who reefed the sails

explanation.surface: Uniform jackets issued to young naval officers.
explanation.walkthrough: Midshipmen are junior naval officers; their nickname comes from reefing sails.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a short heavy sailor's coat and, in naval slang, a midshipman.

clue.text: Folly of head on stop over

indicators.note: turned over means flipped, so the word is read backwards
on means placed next to, so one piece follows the other

blocks.note: to dam is to stop a flow
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness

explanation.surface: The foolishness of a leader who calls a halt to everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Madness can mean extreme foolishness or senseless behaviour, the same as folly.
